business_rules.statement: Publication and packaging are two different acts: publication creates a version; packaging happens once a Workflow is published and a Run assigned, and a package always belongs to exactly one Run.
business_rules.enforcement_point: package generation service at run assignment

business_rules.statement: The package is pinned per Run: the Run executes the package it was assigned, subject only to the adoption rules; in-flight runs are never re-based.
A package that fails device-side validation is never activated and the Run shows a rejection state.
A package containing an unresolved reference is never delivered.
Packages are stored only in the application-managed encrypted store and never in the device gallery or general file storage.
Package expiry never terminates a Run already in progress; expiry governs activation, not continuation.
A revoked package cannot be activated, and a Run already in progress on it continues to completion.
A rollback is executed as a new publication through the full three-stage chain, never as an in-place reversion.
Package eviction occurs only after the Run is complete and synced.
A package failing integrity validation is rejected whole; no part of it is used.
A device newer than the package's minimum application version accepts the package.
A Workflow version is never deleted; archival is manual and blocked while active Jobs reference it.
All four reconciliations produce a raised event on mismatch and never a silent resolution.
business_rules.applies_to: assignment/inventory, commands/acks, captures/record, pinned version/run record

business_rules.statement: An in-progress Run is never rebased by any publication of any class.
No worker notice is forced for a patch version, including a Lane-B auto-published patch.
Expiry of the update window flags the prior version outdated and does not adopt the new version.
Rule 1 — the network is never a safety dependency: every deterministic gate, deviation detection and severity classification runs on-device and is mandatory.
Rule 2 — the oversight surfaces never claim liveness they do not have; the Client Command Center is live to the server's knowledge, and it says so.
Rule 3 — offline is a displayed state, never a hidden failure; this binds the Delivery Operations Hub and the Super Admin platform console as well.
Rule 4 — the Studio requires connectivity and must not imply reach: publication confirmations are worded as publication, never as adoption.
Rule 5 — the worker is never asked to resolve platform state; conflict resolution, work allocation and other workers' data are not in the app.
Rule 6 — configurability may tighten, never loosen: no tenant setting may make any of the above weaker.
No surface renders any element implying a command was delivered to, or applied by, a device whose state is not confirmed by that device's own acknowledgement.
The deterministic safety layer on the device operates identically online and offline, and no platform control suppresses it.
A Severity 1 classification places its hold locally at capture, with escalation delivery deferred to sync.
Hold propagation is displayed as issued, propagating, and in force per device, never as a single completed state.
No element transitions from pending to official without a device acknowledgement.
A run does not display as complete until every assigned device has synced.

The absolute rule: no surface may display, phrase, colour, badge, animate, count, aggregate, export or notify in any way implying an offline tablet received or applied any of twenty-two enumerated artefacts.
business_rules.enforcement_point: all five surfaces; lexical scan in CI
business_rules.applies_to: commands, publications, approvals, role/scope/qualification changes, revocations, suspensions, wipes, hold releases, AI actions/models, configuration and scheduled changes

business_rules.statement: The word "synced" never appears as a standalone state on any surface.
No notification is the sole enforcement mechanism for a hold, qualification, authorisation, approval, suspension or device command.

A scheduled server action affecting an offline tablet remains PENDING until delivery, validation, application, acknowledgement and reconciliation have occurred in order; the scheduled time passing does not prove device application.
The passage of a scheduled time never advances a command state.
Every open scheduled value in this section is carried as TBD — Client Decision Required and no default is applied in code.
Offline behaviour is triggered by sync outcome, never by the operating system link indicator alone.
Media is never evicted in any mode where server receipt cannot be confirmed.
No mode permits a write whose audit event cannot commit in the same transaction.
No function classified fully available offline makes any network call on its execution path.
Designated high-risk actions, sign-offs foremost, force a sync before proceeding.
Trust-window expiry produces a safe stop with all local data preserved, never a silent continuation on stale cache.

No fallback may bypass role-based access control, cross tenants, bypass qualification, specifications, evaluation, approval, publication, or the Severity 1 hold and release rules; nor silently discard or overwrite data; nor present stale data as current or failure as success; nor depend indefinitely on one person; nor enter an infinite retry loop.
business_rules.enforcement_point: fallback register review at each release

business_rules.statement: Every run assigned to a device has exactly one pinned package version for its whole life.
A run whose package has not arrived displays as not-yet-ready and is not enterable.
No package contains Training Library content.
Every package contains the severity mappings, catalog definitions and tenant action bundles needed to classify and act at capture.
Every package contains the platform deviation-capture forms so the default gate-failure path works offline.
No package is generated from content that has not completed the three-stage approval chain.
Publication is blocked where the run's locale is incomplete.
Every measurement screen in a package carries at least one severity mapping.
A pinned package has exactly one outward lifecycle transition, to released.
No authored step may make Training Library content a precondition of advancing.
The package carries content in the run's locale and nothing is translated at runtime.
Manifest scope fields are checked against the device's own assignment before activation, and a tenant mismatch is always fatal.
Package download is never a worker action and never requires worker troubleshooting.
No media object is evicted without both confirmed server receipt and a passed integrity check.
The device never holds data outside the scope its assigned runs require.
No storage-full behaviour and no reserved-capacity threshold is implemented before DEC-STORE-001 is decided.
The activation path fails closed when verification cannot produce a positive result.
A run is never enterable without a verified, pinned package.
Captured work is never discarded by any package failure path.
No capture is ever lost, silently discarded, or silently overwritten by any path in this chapter.
Every conflict, quarantine, cancellation and recomputation produces an audit entry committed in the same transaction as its effect.
A device with a pending suspension or wipe order never uploads under a stale authority: step 7 evaluates before steps 21 and 22 in every run of the protocol.
No step in the protocol can delete a locally committed capture.
business_rules.enforcement_point: static and dynamic analysis of the local capture store

business_rules.statement: The absolute conflict rule: a valid worker capture is never silently overwritten; where last-write-wins would discard one, both values, both timestamps and both workers are preserved and the conflict is recorded.
No conflict resolution lifts, weakens or alters a Severity 1 hold.
Skew-flagged conflicts are excluded from Resolve All (no role may include one).
No capture is rejected, discarded or hidden because of skew.
A tenant cannot set a clock-skew threshold above 60 minutes; the value is rejected, not logged.
No quarantined or dead-lettered record can be deleted by any role, including the Tenant Admin and the root account.
business_rules.enforcement_point: quarantine store; no delete control exists

business_rules.statement: No execution summary, dashboard tile or report includes a quarantined record.
The quarantine write does not occur if its audit entry cannot be committed.
The panel never blocks execution; no run, step or capture waits on conflict review.
Flagging a resolution opens the append-only correction path and never alters the sync result.
Each Resolve All acceptance is individually audited (nine conflicts produce nine audit entries, not one).
No surface, in any state, implies an offline device received or applied a command.
A landed record claiming an unpublished workflow version is quarantined, not accepted.

decisions.question: Whether work packages are signed, where the signing key lives, and whether the device holds a platform public key pinned at enrollment or fetched.
options: no signing, relying on transport security alone
platform-signed packages with a key pinned at device enrollment
platform-signed packages with key rotation and an application-version floor tied to the rotation
decisions.impact: Determines whether a device can prove a package is the one the platform built.

decisions.question: The authoritative field-by-field assignment of package-borne versus server-only values, which §6.7.4 says Part VII carries but Part VII does not enumerate.
options: publish the field-by-field register as a named artefact jointly owned by Part V and Part VII specifications
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until decided: no value outside the seven source-named classes is treated as package-borne.
decisions.impact: The entire Lane B distribution rule depends on it.

decisions.question: Whether a library edit propagates to an in-flight run whose package pinned the prior version, or pinning wins absolutely.
options: pinned-until-run-end / pinning wins absolutely
push-on-next-sync for library items only
split by item class (containment checklists pushed, coaching assets pinned)
library edits to safety artefacts force a republication and a version change
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until decided: pinning holds and no propagation into an in-flight run occurs. §33.7 recommends pinned-until-run-end; §35.7 recommends option (c) republication.
decisions.impact: Determines whether a corrected safety containment checklist reaches a running floor.

decisions.question: Does the package carry all three work-instruction difficulty levels — simple, standard and expanded — or only the level assigned to the executing worker?
options: carry all three levels
carry only the assigned level
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until decided: the package definition carries all levels, and the Frontline renderer selects by worker-profile field.
decisions.impact: Changes package size, substitution behaviour offline, and mid-shift profile changes.

decisions.question: What the device does when storage is genuinely exhausted; storage-full behaviour is deferred to the Frontline Functional Specification per platform.
options: hard stop at a reserved-capacity threshold
degrade capture fidelity
refuse only optional content (evict coaching assets and lazily staged packages first)
block new run entry while allowing the current unit to complete
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation — R&D: layered (c) then (d) then (a). No behaviour is implemented; DEC-STORE-001 remains open.
decisions.impact: Trades line availability against evidence completeness; no defined terminal state today.

decisions.question: The list of named compliance standards that require deletion; the list is owed by the client.
decisions.impact: Deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it.

decisions.question: How long a wipe command may remain pending against an unreachable device, and what happens if the device never returns.
decisions.impact: Sync-then-wipe cannot complete against a dark device; wipe must never report completion.

decisions.question: Whether an approved Lane-B proposal auto-publishing a patch satisfies §5.11.1's requirement of explicit human sign-off at Author, Reviewer and Release Authority.
options: reading favouring §5.11.1 — the Client Command Center decision is a fourth signature, not a missing one
reading favouring §5.16.3 — a patch reaches a device carrying values the Reviewer and Release Authority never saw
decisions.adopted_working_position: This blueprint does not resolve it and does not soften it. Recommendation without prejudice: the Lane-B decision record names decider, current value, proposed value and scope of impact, carried into the auto-published version's history.
decisions.status: open — both readings preserved; decision owner the client's quality lead
decisions.impact: A value a quality engineer never reviewed can reach a tablet without the worker being told.

decisions.question: Relative ordering of capture upload versus command download at reconnection.
options: Interpretation A — commands first
Interpretation B — captures first
Option C — split by urgency: stop class, then captures, then enabling class
decisions.adopted_working_position: Adopted at Option C on 2026-08-14: pass one applies the stop class (suspension in all three states, device de-authorisation and remote wipe, tenant compliance stop); pass two uploads the full durable queue; pass three applies the enabling class (lot release, reassignment or substitution, qualification clearance, version change).
decisions.status: adopted working position — Derived Clarification; ratification remains with the client's platform leadership
decisions.impact: Satisfies both the cache-validity rule and the sync-then-wipe rule simultaneously.

decisions.question: Command expiry horizons per command class.
options: no expiry
a per-class horizon set platform-side
a per-class horizon set per tenant within a platform ceiling
decisions.impact: Prevents applying a two-week-old reassignment to a run that has since finished.

decisions.question: Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective for the sync service.
options: no committed objective at V1, monitored only
an internal engineering target not exposed to tenants
a contractual objective per tier
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required; recommendation (b) at V1 converting to (c)
decisions.impact: Determines redundancy and what may be contractually promised to a regulated tenant.

decisions.question: Maximum offline duration before a device is treated as lost.
options: derive from the credential trust window
derive from the record-finish window
a distinct tenant-set device-lost horizon within a platform ceiling
decisions.impact: Needed by the wipe interaction, stuck-run manual close and fleet alerting.

decisions.question: Retry budget and dead-letter threshold.
options: fixed platform-wide attempt count
time-boxed budget measured server-side
tenant-set budget within a platform ceiling
decisions.impact: Infinite retry loops are prohibited; the budget bounds the only loop in the chapter.

decisions.question: The numeric cap on the visible sync-conflict list.
options: a fixed platform value
a tenant-set value within a platform ceiling
an adaptive cap based on the reviewing session
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required; recommendation (a) at V1
decisions.impact: Too large a cap encourages indiscriminate Resolve All.

decisions.question: Maximum pending duration for a scheduled action aimed at a device.
options: never expire
expire at a fixed horizon with mandatory human review
expire only for non-safety classes
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation — R&D: never expire safety classes (suspension, hold release, wipe); expire non-safety classes only with a mandatory review item in the Client Command Center.
decisions.impact: An action that expires silently is a safety hole.

decisions.question: Delivery retry cadence and limit.
options: fixed interval
exponential backoff with a ceiling
pull-only with no server retry
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation — R&D: pull-only is already the source's model, so the correct control is a backlog age alert rather than a retry limit.
decisions.impact: Unbounded retry is a banned infinite loop.

decisions.question: Misfire and backfill policy for scheduled work.
options: skip
run once on recovery
run every missed occurrence
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation — R&D: run once on recovery for state-bearing schedules; skip for purely informational digests, with the skip recorded.
decisions.impact: A backfilled notification storm harms the worker; a dropped misfire loses a warning.

decisions.question: Command backlog depth limit per device and the back-pressure behaviour.
options: no limit
limit with alert
limit with supersession compaction
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation — R&D: supersession compaction, with every superseded command retained in audit.
decisions.impact: An unbounded backlog on a long-dark device may exceed safe in-order application.

decisions.question: Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective across services.
options: define objectives per service class
define one platform-wide objective
defer to a managed-service agreement
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: per service class, with the device-resident data path stated separately.
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required, raised by §34.6
decisions.impact: No RTO/RPO is asserted anywhere in Chapters 34 or 35.

decisions.question: How a severity action-bundle change reaches devices when the bundle travels inside a pinned work package.
options: package-borne change that auto-publishes a patch version (Lane B machinery)
server-only, accepting that device-side bundle actions lag
a notified change requiring Job Owner adoption
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until decided: the pinned package's bundle governs the run. Recommendation — R&D: option (a).
decisions.status: open — new decision raised by this blueprint
decisions.impact: A tenant tightening its Severity 2 bundle will not affect any run already under way.

decisions.question: Package validity horizon — how long a device may execute a staged work package with no contact.
options: no package expiry, relying on the credential trust window
an explicit package validity horizon in the manifest
tie package validity to the credential trust window so both expire together
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until decided: no expiry is implemented and no value is assumed. Recommendation — R&D: option (c).
decisions.status: open — new decision raised by this blueprint
decisions.impact: A tablet offline for a week executes content nobody could withdraw or correct.

decisions.question: Ratification of the manifest schema, signature algorithm and key custody, the re-pull retry bound, effective-time semantics, and the mid-run revocation resolution where withdrawal conflicts with pinning.
decisions.status: open — new decision raised by this blueprint
decisions.impact: Blocks device-side integrity and withdrawal.

decisions.question: Visibility of a run assigned while the device is entirely offline, which the device cannot show as not-yet-ready because it knows nothing.
options: accept the gap and rely on the Supervisor knowing the device is offline
reconcile the assignment set on reconnection before pulling packages
additionally warn the assigning Supervisor that the target device is offline
decisions.status: open — new decision raised by this blueprint
decisions.impact: Breaks the honest-readiness promise of §7.6.

decisions.question: How soft suspension lifts — on the operator's signal, or automatically on payment.
options: §4.2.4 — lifts on the operator's signal, not on a payment event, with no payment integration existing
§8.9.2 and Part IX — exit is automatic on payment
decisions.adopted_working_position: The operator's signal, delivered to the device as a suspension-class command at its next sync; no payment event is observed. Adopted 2026-08-14.
decisions.status: adopted working position — both source readings preserved
decisions.impact: Determines the soft-suspension exit trigger reaching devices.

decisions.question: Bounds of the record-finish window and run finish semantics.
decisions.impact: Run auto-close at the record-finish window default of 48 hours is contested.

decisions.question: Scheduled feature-control change — no Super Admin user interface for this is described.
decisions.impact: Blocks scheduled feature-control behaviour.

decisions.question: The published minimum device specification, owed by the client.
decisions.impact: Informs the storage-full decision and staging policy validation.

decisions.question: The nobody-on-shift escalation default — escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery.
decisions.adopted_working_position: Carried as an open drafting value; both readings preserved and nothing settles it.
decisions.impact: Governs fallback-of-fallback escalation when no target role is on shift.

decisions.question: The meaning of the Supervisor+ and QM+ plus forms across five additive, non-hierarchical roles.
options: the source's authority matrix uses the plus form
the source states multi-role is additive and audit records identity and action, never acting as role
decisions.adopted_working_position: This blueprint renders plus forms as explicit role lists, preserving rather than resolving the contradiction.
decisions.impact: Determines who may resolve conflicts and take Command Center actions.

decisions.question: Disablement and rollback of a deployed composed agent, and package artificial-intelligence/model compatibility.
decisions.impact: Blocks manifest AI-compatibility field ratification.

contradictions.description: DEC-LANEB-001: §5.11.1 requires explicit human sign-off at Author, Reviewer and Release Authority; §5.16.3 and §6.7.4 have an approved Lane-B proposal auto-publish a patch with no second approval.
conflicting_values: no Workflow content reaches the frontline without explicit human sign-off at each stage
an approved Lane-B proposal auto-publishes a patch version with no second approval and no ceremony

contradictions.description: Consequence of DEC-LANEB-001 that follows from both readings: an auto-published Lane-B patch carries the patch class, and the patch class forces no notice on the worker.
conflicting_values: a value a quality engineer never reviewed can reach a tablet
the worker is not told

contradictions.description: DEC-LIB-001: §5.7 says a library edit propagates to every referencing screen immediately; §5.14 and Part II say a run's package is pinned at assignment and never re-based.
conflicting_values: immediate propagation on save to every referencing screen across every Workflow
the run executes the package resolved at 05:41 until it completes

contradictions.description: DEC-PKGFIELD-001: §6.7.4 states the field-by-field package-borne versus server-only assignment is carried in the package contract of Part VII, and Part VII does not enumerate it.
conflicting_values: carried in the package contract of Part VII
Part VII does not enumerate it

contradictions.description: DEC-SYNC-001: §8.13.1's cache-validity rule argues commands first; §7.11 and §8.13.3's sync-then-wipe rule argues captures first. The source contains one sentence supporting each, neither subordinate.
conflicting_values: the rule that stops a suspended worker continuing on a dark tablet
de-authorising a device must not destroy unsynced work

contradictions.description: DEC-SUSP-001: §4.2.4 says soft suspension lifts on the operator's signal and not on a payment event; §8.9.2 and Part IX give the exit as automatic on payment.
conflicting_values: lifts on the operator's signal, no payment integration exists
exit is automatic on payment

contradictions.description: DEC-OFFASSIGN-001: §7.6 promises a run is shown as not-yet-ready rather than silently missing, but a run assigned while the device is offline is unknown to the device and shows as nothing at all.
conflicting_values: shown as not-yet-ready rather than silently missing
the device displays nothing because it cannot know

contradictions.description: Mid-run package revocation conflicts with version pinning: a run finishes on the version it started on, yet continuing to execute withdrawn content breaches the approval and release-authority rung.
conflicting_values: a run finishes on the version it started on (§7.10.6)
the run is stopped at its current step and captured work is quarantined

contradictions.description: DEC-WIPE-001: remote wipe requires a final sync attempt of pending captures, which an offline device cannot perform; pending duration and never-returns case are unstated.
conflicting_values: every erasure is preceded by a final sync attempt
an offline device cannot perform the final sync

contradictions.description: DEC-PLUS-001: the source's authority matrix uses Supervisor+ and QM+ plus forms, while the source also states multi-role is additive and non-hierarchical and audit records identity and action.
conflicting_values: Supervisor+ / QM+ plus form
multi-role is additive; audit records identity and action, never acting as role

contradictions.description: DEC-BUNDLE-001: §5.14.1 and §7.9.2 place tenant severity action bundles inside the pinned package, while §3.3 has tenants configuring them server-side in the tenant administration area.
conflicting_values: the bundles a tenant configured travel in the Workflow package
tenants configure bundles in the tenant administration area (server-side)

contradictions.description: Superseded position on offline deviation evaluation: an earlier discovery-stage description had offline deviations processed at sync; the binding position is evaluation happens at capture, only escalation delivery happens at sync.
conflicting_values: processed at sync, with severity-band evaluation running on the captured value at that point
evaluation happens at capture; only escalation delivery happens at sync

contradictions.description: DEC-SYNC-001 adopted position supersedes an earlier Recommendation — R&D recorded in the same card, which put version change in the first pass and the stop class last.
conflicting_values: earlier recommendation: version change first, stop class last
adopted: stop class first, version change in phase three

contradictions.description: Compliance-stop capture recovery: §7.11 says the application locks immediately and preserves all local data, while §4.2.3 states only that logins are blocked and in-flight runs stop, and §8.15.2 describes only a server-side compliance-emergency path with nothing about device-held captures.
conflicting_values: preserves all local data
no stated recovery route for device-held evidence

controls.label: Adopt
controls.effect: Adopts a notified-class version for one Job.

controls.label: Adopt all
controls.effect: Adopts the notified-class version across all affected Jobs.

controls.label: rebase-or-keep control per Run
controls.effect: Rebases or keeps a scheduled-not-started Run on adoption.

controls.label: on-demand re-pull
controls.effect: Forces redelivery of a run's work package to a device.

controls.label: Understood
controls.effect: Sole control on the compliant hold-release confirmation dialog.

controls.label: Resolve
controls.effect: Resolves the selected conflict entry individually.

controls.label: Resolve All
controls.effect: Accepts the most recent version of every listed ordinary conflict.

controls.label: Flag this resolution
controls.effect: Opens the append-only correction path; never alters the sync result.

controls.label: release for revalidation
controls.effect: Releases a quarantined record back into the acceptance path.

controls.label: record a permanent disposition with a mandatory note
controls.effect: Permanently dispositions a quarantined record; no delete control exists.

controls.label: manual sync control
controls.effect: Convenience only; sync is never a worker dependency.

controls.label: dismiss control
controls.effect: Dismisses SCR-FL-SYNC-03; no resolve or accept control exists.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Package generation failure (unresolved library pointer, missing locale variant, signing-service failure, generation timeout)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry generation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Supervisor performs an on-demand re-pull; then the Supervisor assigns the worker to a different Run whose package is ready, or the Job Owner keeps the Job on a prior version
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No Run starts without a complete, validated, pinned package
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Correct the underlying content and regenerate; RTO/RPO TBD — Client Decision Required, shift-relative

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A manifest field that cannot be resolved at generation
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Generation fails and is retried
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Underlying content corrected (library item republished with a version); then the Run is assigned on a prior version or not assigned
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No device holds a package it cannot fully validate
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Regeneration; console package inventory shows which manifest versions each device holds

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An interrupted download
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The download resumes automatically on reconnection
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Supervisor on-demand re-pull; then the worker executes a different assigned Run whose package is ready
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No Run executes on a partial package
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Completion of the download and validation; residual risk: storage-full undefined under DEC-STORE-001

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Repeated package rejection on a device (persistent corruption, un-updatable app version, signing key mismatch after rotation)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Redelivery
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Application update through the console-owned release channel; then the device is withdrawn from service and the worker moves to another enrolled tablet
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The worker works on a conformant device; the faulty device holds no active package
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Repair, update, or retirement as an audited device-lifecycle act

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An undecided notified-class adoption (Job Owner left, notification unacknowledged, window elapsed)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The prior version is flagged outdated at window end — a visible signal, not an automatic adoption
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Job Owner field is reassigned and the new owner decides; then Quality Manager or Tenant Admin escalates. The source states no automatic adoption on window expiry and none is invented
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An approved version in force, an outdated flag visible, an undecided adoption on record
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A decision

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Device loses connectivity mid-run
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Degrade to queues and continue the pinned package
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Authored Work Instructions replace agent coaching; then trust-window expiry leads to safe stop
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Application stops the affected path with all local data preserved
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on reconnection, never a worker action; RTO/RPO TBD under DEC-RTORPO-001

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Command cannot reach a device
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The command remains queued and available for delivery, displayed truthfully everywhere
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Authorised human escalation carries the instruction out-of-band and is recorded, but never substitutes for the command
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Held lot, parked run, or unapplied suspension — the conservative state persists
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device contact; backlog depth limit undefined under DEC-SCHED-QUEUE-001

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Oversight surface cannot compute freshness
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Render the last computed freshness with its own age
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Render Unknown
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The element is read-only and dependent actions are disabled with a stated reason
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Freshness inputs return

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Reconnection produces a conflict or a skew flag
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A timestamp outside the skew threshold is not trusted; the event routes to the conflict-and-skew review
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The panel caps the visible list with a count and offers Resolve All; where a Quality Manager is unavailable the conflict remains open and audited and never auto-resolves
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Conflict open, both versions retained, nothing overwritten
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Quality Manager resolution

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Trust window expires with no sync
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Forced re-sync attempt
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Capability tightens to the safe subset; then safe stop of the affected path
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The application preserves all local data and displays the exit condition
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Successful re-sync; no looser option exists and the configurability principle forbids a tenant loosening it

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Package unavailable or not yet staged
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Lazy pull on next connectivity
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Supervisor on-demand re-pull; then supervisor reassigns the run to a device that holds the package
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run remains not-yet-ready and not enterable; the worker continues with other assigned runs
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Staging; RPO trivially zero because no data exists to lose

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Package present but untrustworthy (corruption, tampering, scope mismatch, incompatible version, expiry, revocation)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded re-pull for accidental corruption only
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Supervisor re-pull or reassignment; then application upgrade through the release channel
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run is not enterable with a specific stated reason; captured work under a later-revoked package is preserved and quarantined for Quality Manager disposition
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Corrected package or corrected application build

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Reconnection fails at any of the thirty-seven steps or partially succeeds and then breaks
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Resume from the durable queue at the failed step
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device enters the specific Chapter 37 blocker state and a named human path opens; where nobody of the target role is on shift, escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role marked as a fallback delivery (DEC-NOSHIFT-001)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Device continues offline execution with full local safety; all data retained; sync indicator truthful; no surface claims the device received anything
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Network restoration or the named human act — never a silent retry loop; RTO/RPO TBD under DEC-SYNC-003

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Conflict detected at step 23; object family unclassifiable, both writes skew-flagged, audit write fails, panel unreachable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: An unclassifiable object family defaults to the most conservative rule — preserve both, resolve nothing automatically, route to Quality Manager review
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where both writes are skew-flagged neither may win unreviewed; where the audit write fails the resolution does not occur at all
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Both versions retained, no automatic winner applied, conflict open in the panel, work continuing
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Human resolution, or the append-only correction path

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Clock skew beyond the tenant threshold
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Flag, order by server receipt, suppress automatic conflict resolution
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Individual Quality Manager review of every affected conflict; where the server time source itself is in doubt, no write is granted ordering authority from device time
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: All captures recorded and attributed; conflicts open and individually reviewable; work continuing; the device's clock condition visible in fleet telemetry
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device time correction; the flag persists on historical writes

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A record fails validation and cannot be accepted
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Where the quarantine store is unavailable the record is not accepted and not discarded: it stays queued on the device
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the notification fails the quarantine entry still exists in SCR-DOH-QUAR-01; where volume spikes, back-pressure is applied to the reconnection transfer
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Records retained on the device or in quarantine; figures computed only from accepted data; a named human alerted
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Release and revalidation from step 19, or a recorded permanent disposition with a note

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Sync-conflict review panel unreachable, entry rendering failure, Resolve All partially failing, correction path unreachable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Conflicts remain recorded and auditable in the Delivery Operations Hub; review is delayed, nothing is lost
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Each Resolve All acceptance is individually transactional so the successful subset stands; where the correction path is unreachable the flag is still recorded
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Conflicts recorded, both versions retained, work continuing, review pending
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Panel restoration

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Five-surface convergence failure at step 35
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Recompute the diverging surface from the Hub record and re-compare
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The diverging surface displays its data as stale with an explicit as-of stamp and a convergence exception is raised; where a surface cannot label its own staleness, affected elements are withheld
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The Hub record stands as truth; every other surface agrees, states its lag, or states its unavailability
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Recomputation or remediation of the underlying surface fault
